name: Bardcore

influenced_by: a 2020 wave of "everything is a cover in an old style" YouTube music memes

media.title: Hildegard von Blingin's YouTube channel (2020–)
media.note: widely credited as a key popularizer of the bardcore cover trend

reacts_against: nothing in particular; bardcore is a playful genre exercise — modern pop and dance songs reimagined as if performed by a medieval bard — rather than a reaction to any prior style.
article: Bardcore is unusually easy to date precisely for an internet aesthetic: the trend of reimagining modern pop songs with medieval instrumentation (hurdy-gurdy, lute, recorder) and faux-Middle-English lyrics took off specifically in 2020, spread largely through YouTube channels like Hildegard von Blingin's, which built a substantial audience almost overnight. The joke works because the source songs are usually recognizable despite the stylistic transplant, and the format proved flexible enough to apply to everything from club anthems to heavy metal. A matching visual language followed naturally from the music's premise: illuminated-manuscript borders, parchment textures, tapestry weave and candlelit color, all drawn from genuine medieval and early Renaissance manuscript illumination rather than invented fantasy-medieval imagery. Because the trend is so recent and so clearly traceable to specific 2020 videos, bardcore is one of the best-documented internet aesthetics on this list in terms of origin point, even though the actual visual and musical materials it draws from are centuries old.
